task: Spinal motion segment (functional spinal unit): facet-joint load-sharing & segmental mechanics. Falsifier (symmetric): a disc-only model (ignoring facets, MECHANISM_INTERVERTEBRAL_DISC.md's own scope) must FAIL to reproduce measured facet contact forces AND over-predict disc load in extension; facets must limit axial rotation to measured small segmental ranges (facet-free model over-rotates); segmental ROM per level must match White & Panjabi / measured in-vivo bands (lumbar flexion-extension ~12-17 deg); perturbation adversaries: facetectomy (increases instability/ROM), disc degeneration (shifts load to facets), spondylolisthesis (facet/pars failure -> shear instability).
confidence_tier: Mixed, disclosed per-claim. CADAVERIC-DIRECT-MEASUREMENT-ANCHORED (3 independent techniques -- IVLC-deduction, direct pressure transducer, pressure-film -- across 2 independent labs) for the core facet-load-fraction claim (Yang & King 1984; el-Bohy 1989; Dunlop/Adams/Hutton 1984). IN-VIVO-RADIOGRAPHY-ANCHORED (Pearcy 1984 + Pearcy & Tibrewal 1984, same lab, companion papers) for segmental ROM and coupled motion. CADAVERIC-STRUCTURE-ABLATION-ANCHORED for the 2 perturbation adversaries: facetectomy (Abumi 1990, ROBUST rotation-increase claim confirmed by a 2nd decorrelated 2024 FE study; its SELECTIVITY sub-claim CONTESTED by that same 2024 study, disclosed as an open tension) and spondylolisthesis (Grobler 1994 + Crawford 2001, a 4th independent lab). WHOLE-SPINE-ONLY, no per-region breakdown extracted, for the facet-orientation anatomy anchor (Panjabi 1993) -- the orientation-to-coupled-motion MECHANISM is uncontroversial gross anatomy, not this paper's own per-level numeric table.

decorrelated_anchor: The core facet-load-fraction claim is over-determined across 3 independent measurement TECHNIQUES (intervertebral-load-cell deduction, direct pressure transducer, interposed pressure-film) spanning 2 independent labs (Wayne State: Yang/King/el-Bohy; Bristol: Adams/Hutton/Dunlop), plus a reciprocal disc-pressure trade-off (el-Bohy 1989) that rules out a simple rig-artifact explanation. The segmental-ROM claim is anchored in vivo (Pearcy 1984 + Pearcy & Tibrewal 1984, biplanar radiography) and corroborated by a modern, large-N (1139 FSU), standardized-protocol in-vitro data collection (2025) -- 3 decorrelated modalities (cadaveric pressure/force, in-vivo radiography, modern standardized in-vitro) converging on the same qualitative picture. The 2 perturbation adversaries (facetectomy, spondylolisthesis) are each anchored in dedicated cadaveric structure-ablation studies from labs independent of the load-fraction anchor (Yale/Panjabi-Abumi; Wake Forest/Wilder-Pope), with the facetectomy adversary specifically cross-checked against a 2nd, decorrelated, modern (2024) FE study rather than accepted from one source alone.
honest_gaps: Abumi 1990's exact facetectomy ROM degree deltas not extracted (paywalled, no OA full text found this session) -- only the qualitative mode pattern was used.

Panjabi 1993's per-region (cervical/thoracic/lumbar) facet-angle table not extracted -- only the whole-spine C2-L5 min-max range; a targeted follow-up search did not surface a secondary source with the per-level breakdown.

Facetectomy mode-selectivity is a genuinely open, unresolved tension between Abumi 1990 (extension/lateral-bending spared) and Li/Shih/Chen 2024 (both also increase) -- disclosed, not resolved, kept out of the pass/fail gate tally.
Yang & King's 3-25% normal facet-fraction range is not itself posture-resolved in the available abstract text; the per-posture breakdown sits in a table/figure not extracted this session.
Dunlop 1984's exact per-angle, per-disc-height pressure values were not extracted, only the qualitative direction claims.
The Wilke directional cross-check (Sec 10) is explicitly non-decisive -- confounded by posture-dependent extensor-muscle-force differences; cannot be resolved with Wilke's single-subject dataset.
The twin-worked-example's extension-posture overlay (Sec 11) is illustrative/hypothetical -- subject2 has no extension-posture trial in this repo.
Single lumped lumbar segment scope, consistent with every other spine build in this repo -- no per-level (L1-2 through L5-S1) facet-load-fraction breakdown was modeled.

No finite-element or multibody simulation was built this session -- the model is a literature-anchored quantitative arithmetic comparison plus a geometric mechanism argument, not a new simulated motion segment.

Cervical/thoracic quantitative facet-load-fraction data (the compressive-split analogue of Yang & King's lumbar numbers) was not sought this session -- cervical/thoracic content here is limited to ROM/coupled-motion/orientation contrast.
proposed_cell: facet_disc_load_share_cell: inputs = segment posture angle (flexion/extension, deg) + disc-degeneration grade + total compressive force (from an existing gait/posture cert, e.g. spine_gait_force_results.json); outputs = disc-fraction, facet-fraction (calibrated to Yang & King 1984's [0.03,0.25]->0.47 range), predicted axial-rotation ROM (calibrated to Pearcy & Tibrewal 1984's ~2 deg/level, inflating toward Abumi/FE2024's facetectomy deltas under a 'facet removed' flag), predicted flexion-extension ROM (calibrated to Pearcy et al. 1984's ~14 deg/level). Falsifier gate: disc-only submodel (facet-fraction forced to 0) must fail the [0.03,0.25] containment check (this build's gate1); facetectomy flag must inflate axial-rotation ROM by >=1 decorrelated-study-consistent factor (gate3). Couples directly into MECHANISM_INTERVERTEBRAL_DISC.md's existing P_NP=k(F/A) pressure model by first subtracting the facet-fraction share from F before computing disc pressure -- would let a FUTURE extension-posture trial re-test that doc's own falsifier with the facet split included, instead of assuming 100% disc-transmitted.
